fields.meta_title: Audition Form Template and Builder for Open Calls | Emergent
fields.meta_description: What an audition form should ask, section by section, plus an app that books audition slots and keeps every headshot with the right name.
fields.h1: Build an Audition Form That Runs Your Open Call
fields.hero_description: An audition form tells a director who wants which role and which rehearsals each performer will miss. Emergent builds the form and the table every audition lands in.
fields.features_subheading: Most audition forms that rank are sheets printed and filled in by pen. Emergent keeps those sections and adds what paper cannot.
fields.feature_1:
Contact details and age up front

Collects contact details and age or grade on the first screen. For anyone under 18, it adds a parent or guardian section with their own phone number before any other question.
fields.feature_2:
Roles wanted, and any role accepted

Lists every role in the show with its voice part and lets performers pick the ones they want. A second question, will you accept any role, tells the director who is open to ensemble.
fields.feature_3:
Voice range and dance training

Records voice part and range next to dance styles and years of training. Instruments get their own question, and a director casting an actor-musician show can filter for guitarists.
fields.feature_4:
Rehearsal conflicts as real dates

Asks for conflicts on the rehearsal calendar, not in a free-text box. Every date lands in one table, where the stage manager sees who misses a rehearsal before the cast list goes up.
fields.feature_5:
Headshots and prescreen videos

Accepts a headshot and a prescreen video with the form. Each file saves to storage your company owns, filed under the auditioner's name, and nobody has to sign in to upload.
fields.feature_6:
Your code, in your GitHub

Exports the app and every audition record in its database to GitHub on paid plans. Your developers can host it on your own domain and keep it running from one season to the next.

fields.usecase_heading: Audition Forms for Four Kinds of Company
fields.tab_content_1:
Tech week clashes show up on one calendar

Directors cast around conflicts as much as talent. For its spring musical, Riverbend Players asks every auditioner to mark the rehearsal dates they cannot make. The app checks each date against tech week and flags the 3 auditioners who would miss part of it. The director sees those names before posting callbacks.
fields.tab_content_2:
A guardian signs before the student picks a time

Student auditions start with a guardian, not the student. At Maple Ridge High, a student who fills in the fall play form finds the slot picker locked until a parent or guardian signs. The guardian gets a link by email and signs on a phone. Then the 4-minute slots open for that student to book.
fields.tab_content_3:
Two yes votes send the dancer to callbacks

Prescreen videos cut a long open call down to one day. Applicants for a contemporary dance company's new season upload a 60-second solo with the form. Two reviewers watch each video and vote yes or no. Two yes votes send a callback invitation with a date and studio. A split goes to the artistic director.
fields.tab_content_4:
Names stay hidden until all seats are set

Seating auditions are judged by ear alone. A youth orchestra hears its violinists behind a screen, and the form gives each one a number at check-in. Three judges score every candidate out of 10, and the app ranks them by average. Names appear only after the conductor confirms the seats.

fields.howto_title: How to Create an Audition Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps for a director or stage manager. Settle what you are casting and when you rehearse before the form goes out.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 List the roles you are casting
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Add a guardian step for minors
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down every role with its age range and voice part, and note whether it dances. Mark the roles you will fill from the ensemble. Performers then pick from that list on the form instead of guessing what the show needs.
fields.howto_step_2_des: State the material in the form itself: a 16-bar or 32-bar cut of a song, a short monologue, or a combination taught in the room. Musicals usually ask for one of those two song cuts. Naming which one spares the accompanist a scramble.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Publish the rehearsal calendar with the form and ask for conflicts on it, date by date. Mark tech week and performances as dates nobody can miss. A conflict listed now is a scheduling note; one found in week five can mean recasting.
fields.howto_step_4_des: For anyone under 18, ask a parent or guardian for contact details and a signature before the student books a slot. Put the rehearsal commitment and any fee in the text they sign, not in a separate email they may never open.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Split the audition day into fixed slots and let each performer book one on the form. Hold a few back for walk-ins. Every booking puts a name next to a time, and the panel works through the day from that list.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Give each panelist the same short scale for singing and acting, plus movement if the show dances, with room for a note. Scores saved to each auditioner's record mean callbacks come from numbers the whole panel can see, not from memory.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Pick callbacks from the scored list and send each performer a time and room, with what to prepare. A callback is a second, narrower audition. Tell people what will be different, such as new sides or a partner to read with.

plan.angle: The live top 10 is blank one-page audition forms: community theater and school PDFs (Apex, Seussical, Little Theatre of Mechanicsburg), two Scribd uploads, a college jury evaluation sheet, a Jotform template and a Google Form template. They all ask the same things: contact details, roles wanted, will you accept any role, vocal range, dance and instrument experience, training, a photo and rehearsal conflicts. This page lays out those sections with the reason each one matters to a director, then builds what a printed sheet cannot: a conflict calendar checked against tech week, a parent signature that gates a student's audition slot, video prescreens two reviewers vote on, and seating auditions scored by number with names hidden.
tab_stories: A community theater's spring musical collects every auditioner's rehearsal conflicts as dates; the app checks them against tech week and flags the 3 auditioners who cannot make it before the director posts callbacks.
A high school drama program will not let a student book an audition slot for the fall play until a parent or guardian has signed the form, and the student sees which step is still open.
A contemporary dance company asks applicants to upload a 60-second solo video; two reviewers vote yes or no, and two yes votes send an invitation to the in-person callback.

A youth orchestra hears violin seating auditions behind a screen; candidates appear only as numbers, three judges score each out of 10, and names are revealed after seats are assigned from the averages.
